title: The Rank of Apparition: k ∣ Fₙ ↔ (entry point of k) ∣ n
description: Proves the exact Fibonacci divisibility characterization k ∣ Fₙ ↔ α(k) ∣ n, where α(k) is the rank of apparition (Fibonacci entry point) of k. The characterization from minimality needs no finiteness (via Nat.fib_gcd and Nat.fib_dvd); existence of α(k) for every k ≥ 1 is the substantive input, proved by a pigeonhole/periodicity argument on the pair sequence (Fₙ, Fₙ₊₁) ∈ (ZMod k)², making entryPoint k a genuine computable definition. decide only, no native_decide. 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: The rank of apparition (also called the Fibonacci entry point) $\alpha(k)$ — the least positive index $n$ with $k\mid F_n$ — is a classical object going back to Édouard Lucas (1878), who used the divisibility structure of Fibonacci and Lucas sequences in his primality tests. The governing fact is that Fibonacci is a *strong divisibility sequence*: $\gcd(F_m,F_n)=F_{\gcd(m,n)}$, which makes $\{n:k\mid F_n\}$ a set closed under gcd, hence exactly the multiples of its least element $\alpha(k)$. The rank of apparition underlies the Pisano period, Wall's conjecture on $p^2\mid F_{\alpha(p)}$, and the law $\alpha(p)\mid p-\left(\tfrac{5}{p}\right)$. Mathlib records the strong-divisibility backbone (`Nat.fib_gcd`, `Nat.fib_dvd`) but says nothing about the rank of apparition — neither that every $k\ge1$ divides some positive-index Fibonacci number, nor that this index characterises the whole divisibility set. This entry, the deepest in the `fibonacci-divisibility-oq-07` chain, supplies both: the minimality characterisation (pure gcd algebra, no finiteness) and the existence of $\alpha(k)$ (a pigeonhole/periodicity argument on the pair sequence modulo $k$), giving the unconditional biconditional $k\mid F_n\iff\alpha(k)\mid n$ with 0 sorries and 0 axioms.
overview.problemStatement: Prove the exact Fibonacci divisibility characterisation $k\mid F_n\iff\alpha(k)\mid n$ for every $k\ge1$, where $\alpha(k)$ is the rank of apparition, and construct $\alpha(k)$ as a total computable function by proving its existence — all with 0 sorries, 0 axioms, no `native_decide`.
overview.proofStrategy: Split into a minimality half and an existence half. The minimality half (`dvd_fib_iff_of_least`) needs no finiteness: if $a$ is any least positive index with $k\mid F_a$, then $k\mid F_n\iff a\mid n$ via `Nat.fib_gcd` ($k\mid\gcd(F_a,F_n)=F_{\gcd(a,n)}$ forces $\gcd(a,n)=a$) and `Nat.fib_dvd` for the converse. The existence half (`exists_pos_dvd_fib`) shows the pair sequence $p_n=(F_n,F_{n+1})\in(\mathbb{Z}/k)^2$ is the orbit of $(0,1)$ under the bijective shift $(a,b)\mapsto(b,a+b)$; pigeonhole on the finite square gives a collision $p_i=p_j$, and injectivity of $\text{shift}^i$ propagates it back to $p_0=p_{j-i}$, so $k\mid F_{j-i}$. `entryPoint k := Nat.find` of that existence is then total and computable, and the main biconditional is the minimality lemma instantiated at it.
keyInsights: The Fibonacci strong-divisibility identity $\gcd(F_m,F_n)=F_{\gcd(m,n)}$ (Mathlib's `Nat.fib_gcd`) is the whole engine: it makes the divisibility set closed under gcd, hence the multiples of one least index.

The minimality characterisation `dvd_fib_iff_of_least` needs NO finiteness — it holds for any least positive witness $a$, using only `fib_gcd` and `fib_dvd`, cleanly separating the algebra from the existence question.
The forward direction turns $k\mid F_n$ and $k\mid F_a$ into $k\mid F_{\gcd(a,n)}$; minimality gives $a\le\gcd(a,n)$ and $\gcd(a,n)\mid a$ gives $\gcd(a,n)\le a$, pinning $\gcd(a,n)=a$ so $a\mid n$.

Existence is a periodicity argument: the shift $(a,b)\mapsto(b,a+b)$ is a *bijection* of $(\mathbb{Z}/k)^2$ (inverse $(a,b)\mapsto(b-a,a)$), so the pair sequence is a pure shift orbit and pigeonhole on the finite square forces a repeat.

Bijectivity is what makes the sequence *purely* periodic: injectivity of $\text{shift}^i$ cancels the common prefix of a collision $p_i=p_j$, propagating it back to $p_0=p_{j-i}$ and reading off $F_{j-i}\equiv F_0=0$.

Because existence is a theorem, `entryPoint k := Nat.find …` is a genuine total computable definition, and the concrete entry points ($\alpha(2)=3,\ \alpha(3)=4,\ \alpha(5)=5$) are checked via the minimality lemma without ever evaluating `Nat.find`.

sections.title: Preamble: the rank of apparition, framed
sections.summary: Imports Mathlib and a docstring stating the goal $k\mid F_n\iff\alpha(k)\mid n$, its relation to the modulus-specific corollaries of `fibonacci-divisibility-oq-07` and the dual index-divisibility $F_m\mid F_n\iff m\mid n$, and the two ingredients (minimality characterisation + existence). Notes Mathlib has `fib_gcd`/`fib_dvd` but nothing on the rank of apparition. Opens `namespace` and `open Nat`.

sections.title: dvd_fib_iff_of_least: characterization from minimality
sections.summary: The mathematical core, finiteness-free: for any least positive $a$ with $k\mid F_a$, proves $k\mid F_n\iff a\mid n$. Forward uses `Nat.fib_gcd` + `Nat.dvd_gcd` to get $k\mid F_{\gcd(a,n)}$, then minimality and `gcd_dvd_left` pin $\gcd(a,n)=a$; converse is `Nat.fib_dvd` composed with $k\mid F_a$.

sections.title: fibPair and the bijective shift
sections.summary: Sets up the periodicity argument: `fibPair k n = (F_n,F_{n+1}) mod k`, the shift $(a,b)\mapsto(b,a+b)$ as an `Equiv` of $(\mathbb{Z}/k)^2$ (inverse $(a,b)\mapsto(b-a,a)$), `shift_fibPair` (one step = one shift, via `fib_add_two`), and `fibPair_eq_iterate` (the sequence is the shift orbit of $(0,1)$).

sections.title: exists_pos_dvd_fib: existence via pigeonhole
sections.summary: `exists_pos_dvd_of_pair_eq` cancels the common prefix of a collision $p_i=p_j$ ($i<j$) using injectivity of $\text{shift}^i$ to get $p_0=p_{j-i}$, whose first coordinate gives $k\mid F_{j-i}$. `exists_pos_dvd_fib` then invokes `Finite.exists_ne_map_eq_of_infinite` (pigeonhole: infinite ℕ into finite $(\mathbb{Z}/k)^2$) to produce the collision.

sections.title: entryPoint and the main characterization
sections.summary: Defines `entryPoint k := Nat.find (exists_pos_dvd_fib k)` — total and computable — with `entryPoint_pos`, `dvd_fib_entryPoint`, and minimality `entryPoint_le` from the `Nat.find` API. The main theorem `dvd_fib_iff_entryPoint_dvd` is `dvd_fib_iff_of_least` instantiated at `entryPoint k`: $k\mid F_n\iff\alpha(k)\mid n$ unconditionally for $k\ge1$.

sections.title: Concrete entry points
sections.summary: Three worked examples via `dvd_fib_iff_of_least` (no `Nat.find` evaluation): $\alpha(2)=3$ ($2\mid F_n\iff3\mid n$), $\alpha(3)=4$, and $\alpha(5)=5$ (the fixed point, $F_5=5$). Each checks the minimal witness by `decide` on the small Fibonacci numerals and `omega` on the index bookkeeping.

conclusion.summary: Proves the exact Fibonacci divisibility characterisation $k\mid F_n\iff\alpha(k)\mid n$ for every $k\ge1$, where $\alpha(k)$ is the rank of apparition, constructed as a total computable `entryPoint k := Nat.find …`. The minimality half (`dvd_fib_iff_of_least`) is pure gcd algebra; the existence half (`exists_pos_dvd_fib`) is a pigeonhole/periodicity argument on the bijective Fibonacci shift. Fully verified: 0 sorries, 0 axioms, no `native_decide`.
conclusion.implications: The result upgrades Mathlib's strong-divisibility backbone into a full structural description of each modulus's Fibonacci divisibility set, and packages `entryPoint` as a reusable computable invariant — the springboard for the Pisano period, Wall's conjecture, and the entry-point divisibility law. The clean split (finiteness-free minimality vs. pigeonhole existence) is a reusable template for any strong divisibility sequence.
openQuestions: Can the entry point be related to the Pisano period $\pi(k)$ (with $\alpha(k)\mid\pi(k)$) formally, connecting this to the periodicity of Fibonacci mod $k$?
Does the entry-point law $\alpha(p)\mid p-\left(\tfrac{5}{p}\right)$ for primes $p$ admit a formalisation on top of `entryPoint`?
Can multiplicativity — $\alpha(\mathrm{lcm}(a,b))=\mathrm{lcm}(\alpha(a),\alpha(b))$ — be derived from the characterisation to compute $\alpha$ from prime powers?

crossReferences.description: Parent in the chain: proves modulus-specific corollaries like $2\mid F_n\iff3\mid n$. This entry generalises them to the uniform rank-of-apparition characterisation $k\mid F_n\iff\alpha(k)\mid n$ for all $k$.
Root Fibonacci identities entry; the strong-divisibility backbone (fib_gcd, fib_dvd) used here underlies the same family of divisibility results.
